claims.claim_text: Qwen3.8-Max scored 86.6 on TerminalBench-2.1, ahead of every other model including Fable 5
Qwen3.8-Max posted a leading score of 93.0 on PaperBench, ahead of Fable 5's 88.8

Qwen3.8-Max scored 74.8 on CoWorkBench and 53.4 on JobBench, ahead of its predecessor Qwen 3.7 Max but behind Fable 5

9.summary: According to freepressjournal.in, Qwen3.8-Max scored 86.6 on TerminalBench-2.1 and 93.0 on PaperBench, both times surpassing Fable 5. The same source reports that on the FrontierSWE benchmark, Qwen3.8-Max scored 73.5, trailing behind Opus 4.8 and Fable 5. Freepressjournal.in also states that Qwen3.8-Max achieved 74.8 on CoWorkBench and 53.4 on JobBench, outperforming its predecessor Qwen 3.7 Max but ranking below Fable 5. Additionally, this source notes that Qwen3.8-Max outscored Fable 5 on OSWorld-Verified but scored lower than Fable 5 on MobileWorld.

34.summary: A potential U.S. ban on Chinese open-weight AI models could impose a significant cost on American businesses, which increasingly depend on lower-cost Chinese AI solutions, according to benzinga.com. claims.claim_text: Washington’s concerns over Chinese open-weight AI models intensified after Beijing-based Moonshot AI launched Kimi K3 in late July.
Moonshot's Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion parameters
The Chinese startup Moonshot AI released the world’s largest open-weights model called Kimi K3 with claimed frontier-level performance.

15.summary: The Chinese startup Moonshot AI launched Kimi K3 in late July, a model described as the world’s largest open-weight AI model with claimed frontier-level performance, according to siliconangle.com. Moonshot’s Kimi K3 reportedly has 2.8 trillion parameters, as stated by freepressjournal.in. Washington’s concerns over Chinese open-weight AI models intensified following this release, according to benzinga.com.

claims.claim_text: Chinese researchers are misusing a technique known as model distillation, which involves using outputs and data from powerful teacher models to train smaller student models.
The White House is concerned that model distillation undermines its export controls and infringes on the intellectual property rights of U.S. model makers.

SapienX Inc. co-founder Trevor Koverko stated that Chinese model distillation is best understood as transferring selected capabilities into cheaper, locally controlled systems and does not imply independence from frontier AI.

1.summary: According to siliconangle.com, Chinese researchers are misusing model distillation, a technique where outputs and data from powerful teacher models train smaller student models. The White House is concerned that this practice undermines its export controls and infringes on intellectual property rights held by U.S. model makers, as reported by siliconangle.com. Siliconangle.com also quotes SapienX Inc. co-founder Trevor Koverko, who said Chinese model distillation is best understood as transferring selected capabilities into cheaper, locally controlled systems and does not mean independence from frontier AI.
